stories.title: Senior RSF commander defects in Sudan
stories.body: Siddiq Ander, a senior commander of Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, announced his defection, accusing relatives of RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti) of controlling the group's money, weapons and promotions. He is the latest in a series of 2026 defections, including a lieutenant colonel who left with 300 fighters in October. Drone strikes are now the leading cause of civilian deaths in the war, according to the UN.
stories.why: Splits inside armed groups are a classic intelligence indicator, and Sudan's war affects arms and migration across the Sahel.

cards.front: Who leads Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF)?
cards.back: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo ("Hemedti"); his brother Abdul Rahim is deputy commander.

stories.title: Vance reaches out to Iran as US plans strikes after midterms
stories.body: Vice-President JD Vance sent a letter, through Qatari mediators, to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing direct talks led by Vance. Rezaei said the US tone had changed completely. At the same time, US media reported that the US and Israel have drawn up joint plans to strike Iran after the 3 November midterms. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran and Qatar are working on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US accepts Iran's conditions.
stories.why: The next few weeks decide whether oil prices fall with a deal or spike with renewed war, both of which hit Nigeria's budget.

cards.front: Who is secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (as of October 2026)?

stories.title: Israel heads for coalition talks after hung result
stories.body: With about 90 percent of votes counted, Prime Minister Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was on course for 53 seats and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot for 48, well short of the 61 needed. Arab parties could win a record 19 seats. Eisenkot and Netanyahu have both ruled out a minority government backed by Arab parties. President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders after official results, and Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.
stories.why: A weaker Netanyahu government could change Israel's approach to Gaza and Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria starts writing a new National Security Strategy
stories.body: National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu inaugurated a 33-member committee to review the 2019 National Security Strategy and draft a new one, NSS 2026. It is chaired by retired Major General Sarkin Bello and must submit a final draft by 27 November. The new strategy is meant to address terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, cybercrime and misinformation.
stories.why: The National Security Strategy is the framework the NIA and other agencies work within, so it is a likely interview question.

cards.front: Which National Security Strategy is Nigeria replacing, and with what?
cards.back: The 2019 NSS, with a new NSS 2026 (committee inaugurated by NSA Ribadu in October 2026).

stories.title: Hunters fight off bandits in Katsina
stories.body: Katsina State authorities said local hunters killed 14 suspected bandits who attacked travellers in Bakori LGA on 23 October. A traveller was burnt in his vehicle and one hunter was killed. Officials said the attackers, about 26 men on 13 motorcycles, were heading towards Dawan Laila forest. The state warned of possible reprisals; Premium Times could not independently verify the figures.
stories.why: Communities arming themselves is a sign of how stretched formal security is in the North-west, and it raises the risk of reprisal violence.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine and US to meet in Abu Dhabi in November
stories.body: The Kremlin said three-way talks are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. Putin wants talks on long-term security arrangements rather than a short truce, and Russia still demands territory and no NATO membership for Ukraine. Zelenskyy wants strong security guarantees, ten years of funding for Ukraine's army and European involvement. Both sides exchanged 270 prisoners of war, and Ukraine says more than 19,000 civilians have been killed since 2022.
stories.why: A settlement would shift world grain and fuel prices that feed Nigerian inflation.

cards.front: When and where are US–Russia–Ukraine talks planned (as of late October 2026)?
cards.back: The first half of November 2026, in Abu Dhabi.
